name: Wellington

the Wellington Green and State Road 7 corridor
kitchen_profile: polo and golf club dining rooms
intro: Wellington's food economy changes with the horses. From January through April, the Winter Equestrian Festival and polo season turn the village into an international hospitality operation — VIP tents, sponsor pavilions, club dining rooms, and private chefs cooking for the sport's wealthiest owners — then the covers settle back to a polished suburban baseline around Wellington Green and the Forest Hill corridor.

Seasonal whiplash is a produce-supply problem, and it is one we plan for. Event caterers and club kitchens hold a baseline standing order and layer show-week volume on top by the midnight cutoff; specialty items — microgreens, edible flowers, tasting-menu produce — ride the same trucks as the staple cases. The run from Pompano Beach takes about forty-five minutes across the county.
route_note: About 45 minutes from our Pompano Beach warehouse — village and showgrounds stops run daily, with show-season step-ups from January through April.

faqs_unique.q: Can you handle Winter Equestrian Festival and polo season volume?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Event caterers and club kitchens layer show-week volume on a standing baseline by the midnight cutoff — season step-ups are planned into the Wellington route every winter.

faqs_unique.q: Do you supply VIP hospitality and private chefs during show season?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Specialty and tasting-menu produce — microgreens, edible flowers, premium fruit — delivers alongside staple cases, with split cases so precise menus stay precise.

cta_text: Tell us your needs for equestrian-season volume, club service, catering, or neighborhood dining, and we will help build a produce plan around your Wellington schedule.
